subject: Model-Implied Variance of Endogenous Variable Differs Between Two SEM-models with Identical Measurement Models

messages.author: ef14f0685658b5f7
messages.subject: Model-Implied Variance of Endogenous Variable Differs Between Two SEM-models with Identical Measurement Models
parts:
Hi there,

I am running 2 SEMs with identical measurement models with one model having 2 additional exogenous predictors.
However, the R² of the latent variable that I want to predict is smaller in the full model (M2) in comparison with the reduced model (M1) (.132 vs. .141).
Therefore, to check how this happened, I calculated the R² of the dependent latent variable by hand in both models with the following formula: 1 - (residual variance/total variance). These are the results:

M1: 1 - (0.443/0.516) = 0.141
M2: 1 - (0.442/0.509) = 0.132

My question concerns the total (model-implied) variance of this latent variable. How is it possible that it differs between both models?

Estimator = MLR
Missing = FIML
Dataset = identical, there are no extra missings in the full model.


I hope my question is somewhat clear.

Thanks in advance,
Jef
